transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been having some trouble keeping track of conversations lately. 

Like, at the museum where I help out, people will be talking right to me about the next art walk or something. I’ll be looking right at them, but then I realize I completely missed the middle part of what they just said. I end up having to stop them and ask them to run it by me again. It's just been happening enough that I figured I should come in and talk to somebody about it.
When this happens, does it feel like you heard the sound of the person talking but couldn't make sense of the words?

No, I wouldn't really say it's like that. I hear them fine, and I understand the words just fine. It's more that... well, my mind just drifts off somewhere else for a minute. I'm looking right at them, but my thoughts are just on something else entirely, so I just don't catch what they actually said.
Do you remember having this same kind of drifting-off problem when you were a child?

Yeah, actually, I do. Even way back in grade school... I remember my report cards would always say things like "daydreams" or "needs reminders to finish work." And my mother, she actually used to have to sit right beside me at the table just to keep me on track with my homework. She had to do that until I was... well, at least before I was twelve. So, yeah, it's been happening for a long time.
Outside of conversations, do you also have trouble staying focused when you're doing tasks like paperwork, reading, or paying bills?

Yeah, I do. Especially with reading. I can sit down with, say, a gallery packet or a set of notes, and I'll start out fine. But after a few minutes... well, my eyes just keep moving over the page while my mind has completely wandered off. I end up having to go back and read the same part over again just to actually get what it says.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?

No, not really. I mean, I don't really have a lot of complicated tasks to organize these days anyway, since I'm not working. But even when I have things to do around the house, I wouldn't say I have trouble getting them organized. I can figure out what needs to be done and put things in order just fine.
Do these attention problems also cause difficulties for you at home?

No, not really. I mean, my wife handles most of the bills and things like that, so I don't have too many big responsibilities around the house that get messed up. Sometimes I might forget to take out the trash right away if I get distracted, but it's nothing that causes any real problems or arguments at home.
Did these concentration problems start after a stroke, head injury, or another medical illness?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had a stroke or any head injuries, and I don't have any major medical illnesses that I know of. It's just... always kind of been this way, I guess.
Have these attention problems ever caused you significant trouble at work?

Well, I'm retired now, so I don't have a regular job. But I do volunteer with a local museum group, and... yeah, it's caused some issues there. The group has actually had to quietly shift some of the planning pieces away from me because I just couldn't keep track of it all. And I've stopped feeling confident leading the art walks the way I used to, so I've stepped back from that, too. It's frustrating.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?
No, not really. I don't feel restless or have to move around a lot. I'm perfectly fine just sitting still.
Do you often lose things you need for tasks, like keys, glasses, papers, or your phone?

Yeah, I do. Especially with the museum group. I’m always putting down the camera battery, or the name tags, or the envelope with the sign-up sheets... I'll tell myself I'm putting them somewhere safe, and then I just end up spending half the morning retracing my steps trying to find them again.
Do you have the same kind of attention problems in other settings too, like during hobbies or social situations?

No, not really. Um, besides the museum group, I haven't really noticed it causing problems. If I'm just at home doing my own thing or visiting with friends, I do fine. It doesn't seem to be an issue then. It really just comes up when I have to organize things or keep track of details like I was saying.
Have these attention problems ever caused problems in your relationships with family or close friends?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Like I mentioned a minute ago, visiting with friends is fine. And with my family... well, they haven't complained about it. It hasn't caused any real arguments or problems between us.
Do you ever have this same drifting-off problem when watching television?
No, not really. If I'm watching a show or a movie, I can usually just sit and watch it fine. I don't really drift off or lose track of what's happening on the screen.
When you’re having a one-on-one conversation with a friend or family member, do you also find your mind wandering and miss parts of what they’re saying?

Well, with my family or close friends, it's usually fine. But, actually, what really brings me in is that people at the museum will be talking right to me about, say, the next art walk... and I'll be looking right at them, but then I realize I completely missed the middle of what they were saying. I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. So it happens there, just not so much at home.
